The absence of B symptoms (fever, night sweats), endocrine, GI, or psychiatric symptoms makes alternative diagnoses (e.g., lymphoma subtypes like mantle cell, autoimmune disorders, occult infection, or endocrinopathy) less likely. The cytopenias are best explained by bone marrow infiltration and/or immune-mediated mechanisms intrinsic to CLL/SLL. Tobacco use is a comorbidity but not causative of this lymphoproliferation. Staging and prognostic testing are indicated, but the diagnosis itself is definitively established by morphology, immunophenotype, and clinical context.

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia / Small Lymphocytic Lymphoma
